title: Switching a part on shows its settings straight away
goal: Ticking Border, or any other part of a shape, puts its settings behind a second step: a chevron you have to open, and once open the settings sit indented under the row. Ticking a part is already the person saying they want it, so its settings should simply be there, on the line below, in the same column as everything else. No arrow to press, nothing to remember to expand, no indent.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-06, immediately after the Appearance list shipped (one-way-to-add-colour-and-remove-any-part-of-a-s). What is there now, from a read of Sources/Photonz/PartsInspector.swift: a part row draws a chevron when it is on and has settings (opens at line 86), the settings render only when that part is the one open (line 132, gated on openPart matching the row at line 38), and both the settings and the note are indented by the label column width (lines 130 and 134). So there are three things to undo: the chevron, the single open part rule, and the indent. The single open part rule is the one worth thinking about rather than deleting blindly, since it was presumably there to keep the panel short; the user has asked for every on part to show its settings, so the panel gets taller and that is accepted, but check it still reads at a small window height and say so in the audit. The reach note under a row keeps its own indent question: decide whether it follows the settings out to the margin or stays as it is, and say which.
acceptance: Ticking a part shows its settings immediately, directly beneath its row, with no chevron and no second click
Unticking a part hides them again, and the settings never linger for a part that is switched off
The settings line up in the same columns as the rows above and below, with no indentation of their own
Only one part can be open at a time is no longer a rule: every switched on part shows its settings at once, so two parts that are both on are both readable without hunting
The panel does not jump or reflow awkwardly as parts are switched, and a long list of switched on parts scrolls rather than squeezing
Switching a part on and off repeatedly leaves the panel exactly as it started
Audit written under queue/audits/ with one part on, three parts on, and all off, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The ask is unambiguous and I agree with it, so nothing to send back: the chevron was a second step in front of a decision the tick had already made. The one thing worth arguing was what tells a part row apart from a settings row once the indent is gone, since a slider's label wears the same size and colour as a part's name. Answer: the tick column. Only a part row has a checkbox and a colour well at fixed x, and no settings row does, so the list still reads as parts with things under them. Backed up by proximity rather than a step to the right: 16 pt between parts, 6 pt from a row to its own settings. Kept it to that; did NOT restyle the settings labels, which would have been inventing a second typography rule for the same list.

Built. Sources/Photonz/PartsInspector.swift: chevron view, its playtest control, the title tap gesture, the openPart @AppStorage and its key are all gone; settings render whenever the part is on and has settings; the leading padding is off both the settings and the reach note. Outer VStack spacing 10 -> 16 so the gap between parts beats the gap inside one. PlaytestSetupRunner no longer forgets inspector.openPart (the key no longer exists). Scripts/playtest/one-outline-two-kinds-walk.json dropped its 'press Settings in Outline' step, since there is nothing to press.

Second adversarial pass, on the probe. Found the shadow's settings started FURTHER from the Shadow row (14 pt) than Width sits from Outline (6 pt): ShadowInspector still drew the line its own switch used to sit on, empty, and an empty line still takes its spacing both sides. Fixed in LayersPanel.swift by skipping that line when it holds nothing, which is when the switch is borrowed by the parts row and the layer has no shadow override to revert. After the fix both gaps measure the same in the panel dump (Outline 470 -> Width 432, Shadow 399 -> Blur 361).

Verified against every acceptance item with real window captures, Screen Recording granted. New walk Scripts/playtest/parts-settings-inline-walk.json: as-drawn shows Outline's Width with no press and no Settings control anywhere in the dump; three-on shows Width AND all five shadow sliders at once; all-off shows three switches and nothing else, no colour wells or sliders left behind; back-as-drawn is byte-for-byte the same control list and the same y for every row as as-drawn, so switching on and off repeatedly leaves the panel as it started. Column alignment: Appearance's Width and shadow sliders sit at x=1148, the same x as the Effects sliders, which is the full section width, so there is no indent left. A second run at 1160x640 with everything on kept full row heights and pushed Direction and Opacity below the fold, so the dock scrolls rather than squeezes. Suite green at 4240; one-outline-two-kinds walk still ok at 48 steps.

Decided the reach note question the task left open: the note follows the settings out to the margin. Checked it on a mixed two-box selection, where it reads in line with the Position & Size note, the Appearance caption and the Effects note, so the whole dock has one left edge for anything a row says about itself. Doc updated: docs/design/shape-parts.md 'The panel'. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-06-parts-settings-inline.json with three real captures.
